page.text:
A *proof by cases* (or disjunction elimination) establishes a conclusion
$C$ under a set of alternative hypotheses $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_k$ whose
disjunction $A_1 \lor A_2 \lor \dots \lor A_k$ is known to be true. To
succeed, the argument must demonstrate that $A_i \implies C$ for each
individual index $i$.

The cases need not be mutually exclusive, but they must be strictly
*exhaustive*: failure to account for an edge case invalidates the entire
proof. In constructive mathematics, a proof by cases must provide an
algorithm for determining which case holds and how the witness is
extracted.
